result.summary: The page is largely well-structured, but there is one clearly broken data value (a “-100%” discount badge) plus a few smaller inconsistencies: the favorite/heart control is styled differently between cards, the “Fastest near you” cards omit rating/cuisine metadata shown elsewhere, and the search placeholder has weak contrast.

issues.description: The second card in “Popular right now” shows a promotion badge reading “−100%”. A 100% discount implies the item is free, which is almost certainly invalid promo data (or a sign/formatting bug) and undermines trust in the offers shown.
issues.suggestion: Validate discount values server-side and clamp/reject implausible percentages (e.g., >90%). Render realistic values such as “−20%” and hide the badge entirely when no valid promotion exists.

issues.description: The favorite (heart) button is inconsistent between cards: on the ramen card it is a bare white outline sitting directly on the photo, while on the pizza card it has a dark circular scrim behind it. On light imagery the bare icon would be hard to see.
issues.suggestion: Apply the same circular semi-transparent dark background (and identical size/position) to the heart button on every restaurant card for consistent affordance and legibility.

issues.description: Cards in “Fastest near you” show only name and delivery fee, while “Popular right now” cards show rating, time, fee and cuisine. The missing rating/cuisine metadata makes the two rows feel inconsistent and gives users less decision information in the first row.
issues.suggestion: Use a shared card metadata template so all restaurant cards display rating and cuisine (or intentionally document the compact variant), keeping information density consistent across sections.

issues.description: The search field placeholder “Restaurants, dishes, groceries” is light gray on a very light gray fill, giving low contrast that may fail WCAG 1.4.3 for users with low vision.
issues.suggestion: Darken the placeholder text (e.g., #6B7280 or darker) or lighten the field background so the text reaches at least a 4.5:1 contrast ratio, and ensure the icon has an accessible label.
